summary: Conversation cursors now contain four numbers instead of three. Existing cursors take one cursor-gap resync on upgrade; the refreshed conversation then follows normally. Native assistant cost is counted once per message and loaded stui content stays on its individual Simple-density tool row.

replay.detail: The cursor resync refreshes the conversation view, not the claim log. No claim replay or projection rebuild is added. Content loading and usage metadata remain memory-only read projections.

schema.detail: No database tables, indexes, migrations or client schema fields change. The cursor remains an opaque string in the existing contract.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention or fleet coordination rules change.

compatibility.detail: The numeric conversation-cursor suffix changes from store_index.local_position.native_sequence to store_index.local_position.native_sequence.source_generation. Three-number cursors receive cursor-gap with full_resync=true on upgrade. Clients reload the newest authorized conversation page once and continue using its four-number cursor. The added source generation fences in-place transcript rewrites. Assistant message metadata uses one existing block metadata field, including for tool-call-only messages; no schema fields are added, removed or renamed.

downtime.detail: No coordinated outage or migration wait is added; an existing conversation follower performs one cursor-gap refresh after upgrade.

manual.detail: No configuration or manual data migration is required. Clients use the existing cursor-gap resync path and must treat conversation cursors as opaque strings.

recovery.detail: No durable state changes. Swapping binaries requires only the existing conversation resync path when a retained cursor is incompatible; fetched JSON, images and usage projections stay in memory.
